body:
It is specific to Vue, as it verifies `sendEvent` is exposed to the default slot. I don't think it can be moved to the CTS.

The existence of `sendEvent` in the render state is asserted in `connectMenu-test.ts` but it doesn't go much further.

There's still a Vue-specific test asserting the availability of `sendEvent` in the default slot, which cannot be moved to the CTS (see https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/pull/5825/files#r1307453493), and it tests custom slots rendering, which I was not sure we should remove.

Based on your comment I'll remove the custom slots ones, but I'll need to keep this file for `sendEvent`.

Indeed, the name of the directory is misleading because it looks like they're just UI components, but they're really widgets.

If we're stripping away many tests, maybe we could rewrite the few remaining ones so they look more like how users use the APIs (like we do in `react-instantsearch`), e.g., with [Vue Testing Library](https://testing-library.com/docs/vue-testing-library/examples)? Right now the tests feel very internal.

I think for the scope of this PR, leaving the insights tests only might not warrant the introduction of another testing library, but totally agree on the idea of having tests that are designed to follow more closely what users are expected to do.
